heroSummary: The Creality K1 Max handles Sunlu PETG exceptionally well right out of the box, reaching safe speeds up to 179 mm/s capped by a 15 mm³/s volumetric flow limit. While the stock hardened steel nozzle easily sustains the target 240°C temperature, keeping the top lid cracked or the front door vented is recommended to prevent heat creep.
bedSurfaceRecommendation: Textured PEI Plate with PVP glue stick or liquid release agent to prevent permanent surface bonding
slicerTweaks: Cap Max Volumetric Speed at 15 mm³/s under Filament Settings to prevent under-extrusion at high CoreXY travel rates.
Enable Wipe While Retracting with a distance of 1.0 mm to clean up Sunlu PETG ooze before non-print travels.
Set Pressure Advance to 0.045 s (fine-tune via line test) to eliminate corner bulging and seam blobbing on direct drive.
Reduce Auxiliary Part Cooling Fan to 0% and keep main part cooling fan between 20-50% to maintain layer bonding.

troubleshootingMatrix.issue: Severe Stringing and Branching Across Gaps
troubleshootingMatrix.rootCause: PETG is highly hygroscopic and tends to ooze when saturated with ambient moisture or over-retracted.
troubleshootingMatrix.exactFix: Dry the filament in a dedicated dryer at 65°C for 6 hours; increase travel speed to 350 mm/s and enable 'Avoid Crossing Walls'.

troubleshootingMatrix.rootCause: Insufficient top solid layers combined with low part cooling airflow over bridging infill.
troubleshootingMatrix.exactFix: Increase top shell layers to 5, set top surface flow ratio to 0.96, and ensure cooling reaches 50% on bridge and solid infill layers.

troubleshootingMatrix.issue: PEI Coating Tearing Away on Part Removal
troubleshootingMatrix.rootCause: PETG creates an overly aggressive molecular bond directly with hot PEI sheets.
troubleshootingMatrix.exactFix: Apply a uniform layer of PVP glue stick as a sacrificial release barrier, and wait until the bed cools to under 30°C before removing parts.

faq.question: Should the Creality K1 Max door and lid be kept closed for Sunlu PETG?
faq.answer: Keep the top lid slightly vented or remove it entirely; PETG prints best without excessive chamber heat, which can lead to extruder heat creep.

faq.question: Why is print speed limited to 179 mm/s when the K1 Max can go up to 600 mm/s?
faq.answer: Sunlu PETG has a melt-rate bottleneck around 15 mm³/s, which geometrically limits standard 0.4mm nozzle lines (0.2mm height, 0.42mm width) to 179 mm/s without under-extruding.

faq.question: Does Sunlu PETG require a hardened steel nozzle on the K1 Max?
faq.answer: No, standard Sunlu PETG is non-abrasive, though the K1 Max's stock hardened steel nozzle handles it effortlessly with an extra 5°C offset if needed for thermal conductivity.

faq.question: How do I avoid nozzle build-up and burnt brown specks?
faq.answer: Slightly increase your Z-offset by 0.02mm to avoid dragging the nozzle through the molten track, and reduce extrusion multiplier to 0.98.
